newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize seeks places, partners in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize seeks places, partners in Asia.

text.p: Belgian food retailer Delhaize, aware that it has been slow off the mark, is looking for places and partners in Asia, particularly the south east, the company's chief executive officer Gui De Vaucleroy said on Wednesday.
"I hope that in the coming months we will be present in Asia," he told a seminar of Belgian financial analysts. "We have studies under way.
"It is our intention in Asia to work with local partners," he added in reply to a question. He did not say which countries were being scrutinised or if any specific partners had been identified.
Outside Belgium, Delhaize, the country's second largest retailer, is present in the United States through its Food Lion chain as well as in France, Greece and the Czech Republic.
The company said last month consolidated turnover rose by 11.7 percent to 411.6 billion francs last year. It expected consolidated profit to be up by between 15 and 20 percent.
It expected growth in 1997 to continue, in part due to the planned opening of 200 more sales outlets. The firm had 1,700 sales outlets at the end of 1996.
